programme.title: Split
programme.desc: Ex-FBI agent Will Graham (Edward Norton) is an expert investigator who quit the Bureau after almost losing his life in the process of capturing the elusive Dr. Lecter (Anthony Hopkins). After a series of particularly grisly murders, Graham soon realizes that the best way to catch this killer, known as the Tooth Fairy, is to find a way to get inside the killer's mind. For Graham, that means confronting his past and facing his former nemesis, the now-incarcerated Lecter.

Susan contacts a dating agency, but the man that they set her up with turns out to be a bit stiff.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: In part 1 of two episodes, Dr. Phil meets Cheryl, her ex-husband, Dave, and their youngest daughter, Stephanie, who say oldest daughter Cassie has been a drug addict and an alcoholic for years and needs an intervention. One source of contention is the allegation that Dave not only did drugs with Cassie but also received money from her that she admittedly earned through prostitution. Dave counters that, despite using drugs with Cassie twice, he did not encourage Cassie to be a prostitute and he gave back the money Cassie earned through prostitution. Dave contends that he is actually fighting for Cassie’s sobriety and has helped save her life by giving her a home to live in. Things take an uncertain turn when Cassie decides to leave the studio one hour before the taping and run down Melrose Avenue to a liquor store with staffers chasing her. Will Cassie ever make it to stage to talk to Dr. Phil?

While August dismisses the teen’s lethal behavior as "playful," Daisha finds herself trapped in a house with a son who may be a killer. As she plots to conceive a biological heir, a series of dark secrets and "accidents" leave the family’s survival in question.

programme.desc: Narrated by Norman Fell, this anthology follows three seemingly unconnected individuals as each of their lives are disrupted by anomalous entities. Alex buys a talking antique car that has very exorbitant demands. Frank makes friends with a cultivating mold man that lives in his refrigerator. Susan contacts a dating agency, but the man that they set her up with turns out to be a bit stiff.

programme.title: Dr. Phil
programme.desc: In part 1 of two episodes, Dr. Phil meets Cheryl, her ex-husband, Dave, and their youngest daughter, Stephanie, who say oldest daughter Cassie has been a drug addict and an alcoholic for years and needs an intervention. One source of contention is the allegation that Dave not only did drugs with Cassie but also received money from her that she admittedly earned through prostitution. Dave counters that, despite using drugs with Cassie twice, he did not encourage Cassie to be a prostitute and he gave back the money Cassie earned through prostitution. Dave contends that he is actually fighting for Cassie’s sobriety and has helped save her life by giving her a home to live in. Things take an uncertain turn when Cassie decides to leave the studio one hour before the taping and run down Melrose Avenue to a liquor store with staffers chasing her. Will Cassie ever make it to stage to talk to Dr. Phil?

One source of contention is the allegation that Dave not only did drugs with Cassie but also received money from her that she admittedly earned through prostitution. Dave counters that, despite using drugs with Cassie twice, he did not encourage Cassie to be a prostitute and he gave back the money Cassie earned through prostitution. Dave contends that he is actually fighting for Cassie’s sobriety and has helped save her life by giving her a home to live in. Things take an uncertain turn when Cassie decides to leave the studio one hour before the taping and run down Melrose Avenue to a liquor store with staffers chasing her. Will Cassie ever make it to stage to talk to Dr. Phil?

programme.title: TurboZaurs
programme.desc: Jenny and her best friend Blam the Teddy Bear run a magic shop in the town of Dreamville, where everybody can come for magical help. The residents of Dreamville always leave the shop thanking Jenny, but actually, they set the stage for their own miracles, leaving behind in the shop whatever is keeping them from living life and making decisions. After all, the ability to change yourself is the truest form of magic. Jenny and Blam never refuse to help anyone, but it often happens that they’re the ones who need help, since Jenny’s still a kid and Blam’s an eccentric teddy bear.

The residents of Dreamville always leave the shop thanking Jenny, but actually, they set the stage for their own miracles, leaving behind in the shop whatever is keeping them from living life and making decisions. After all, the ability to change yourself is the truest form of magic. Jenny and Blam never refuse to help anyone, but it often happens that they’re the ones who need help, since Jenny’s still a kid and Blam’s an eccentric teddy bear.

The residents of Dreamville always leave the shop thanking Jenny, but actually, they set the stage for their own miracles, leaving behind in the shop whatever is keeping them from living life and making decisions. After all, the ability to change yourself is the truest form of magic. Jenny and Blam never refuse to help anyone, but it often happens that they’re the ones who need help, since Jenny’s still a kid and Blam’s an eccentric teddy bear.

The residents of Dreamville always leave the shop thanking Jenny, but actually, they set the stage for their own miracles, leaving behind in the shop whatever is keeping them from living life and making decisions. After all, the ability to change yourself is the truest form of magic. Jenny and Blam never refuse to help anyone, but it often happens that they’re the ones who need help, since Jenny’s still a kid and Blam’s an eccentric teddy bear.

A brilliant illustrator, author of "L'Arabe du futur" and "Les Cahiers d'Esther", he captures childhood like no one else and has transformed his personal story into a universal work. Also a director, Riad Sattouf is our guest. We also have with us one of the greatest artists of her generation, who has conquered the most prestigious museums. Éva Jospin transforms cardboard, silk or bronze into monumental forests and landscapes, with exceptional technical mastery. And then David Hockney is on show in Belgium, at the Mons Museum of Fine Arts: this is Alex Vizorek's Vizorek'xpert column!

A brilliant illustrator, author of "L'Arabe du futur" and "Les Cahiers d'Esther", he captures childhood like no one else and has transformed his personal story into a universal work. Also a director, Riad Sattouf is our guest. We also have with us one of the greatest artists of her generation, who has conquered the most prestigious museums. Éva Jospin transforms cardboard, silk or bronze into monumental forests and landscapes, with exceptional technical mastery. And then David Hockney is on show in Belgium, at the Mons Museum of Fine Arts: this is Alex Vizorek's Vizorek'xpert column!

A brilliant illustrator, author of "L'Arabe du futur" and "Les Cahiers d'Esther", he captures childhood like no one else and has transformed his personal story into a universal work. Also a director, Riad Sattouf is our guest. We also have with us one of the greatest artists of her generation, who has conquered the most prestigious museums. Éva Jospin transforms cardboard, silk or bronze into monumental forests and landscapes, with exceptional technical mastery. And then David Hockney is on show in Belgium, at the Mons Museum of Fine Arts: this is Alex Vizorek's Vizorek'xpert column!
